Subject: Q2 check-in: usage heatmap & model mix questions

Hey Vivek —

Thanks for the quick onboarding earlier this quarter. I've attached a small heatmap and our internal cost workbook so you can see the recent pattern. Quick summary from our side:

- Token consumption (90d rolling): ~2.1B tokens
  - Embeddings: ~1.47B (70%)
  - Generation: ~630M (30%)
- Monthly spend trend: March run-rate ~= $48k/mo (hosted)
- Latency: avg 320ms, p95 ~720ms for gen endpoints

We're approaching the end of our pilot and starting to look at a renewal + capacity plan. Primary asks:
1) Can you validate whether the model mix and latency are expected for our workload?
2) What uplift / commit profile would materially reduce unit cost while keeping p95 latency under ~800ms?
3) Any quick wins on model selection or quantization you recommend before we sign a longer term commitment?

Attachments: usage_heatmap_q1.png (image/png), cost_model_q1.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

If it helps, happy to do a 30-min playback next week — we can share internal eval prompts and a sample production trace.

Subject: Re: Q2 check-in: usage heatmap & model mix questions

Elena — thanks for the data and the clear asks. Quick playback after scanning the heatmap + workbook:

1) Model mix / latency
- Your embedding-heavy mix explains the spend profile; embeddings are more predictable in latency, generation accounts for most p95 spikes.
- p95 ~720ms is consistent with an NVidia A100-backed hosted service at your gen token sizes, especially with short bursts.

2) Cost levers we recommend (short + medium term):
- Move non-latency-critical embedding batches to a quantized v2 embedding model (we've seen ~25–35% CPU/GPU cost improvement with <1% recall degradation in our benchmark).
- For generation: enable continuous batching on your traffic path and pin a midsize quantized variant for background scoring. That can shave ~10–18% off gen token costs.

3) Renewal / uplift options (ballpark):
- 12mo term, +25% commit (prepaid monthly equivalent) -> ~18% effective unit discount vs hosted pay-as-you-go
- 24mo term, +40% commit -> ~26% discount + priority burst capacity (useful for launch windows)

Operational proposal: start with a 12mo commit for embeddings (since they are the bulk of spend) and keep generation on a flexible pool with automatic fallback to dedicated quantized nodes for heavy scoring. That preserves latency SLOs while optimizing unit economics.

I've sketched a short internal note with proposed uplift math and a staged rollout plan — attaching as redwood_uplift_note.pdf. If you want, I can convert numbers into a formal quote and include an SLA addendum for p95 latency.

Next step: are you available Tue or Wed next week for a 30-min sync? If so, we'll bring Karthik (pricing) and Soojin (ops) to map the rollout.

Cheers,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
